evals.prompt: who does https://www.linkedin.com/in/dvdhsu know? mostly I want to see which of those people work at Stripe or Figma today.
evals.expected_output: A tiered .xlsx of the people the target plausibly knows, each row with verbatim evidence and a current employer, plus a report that leads with the tier table and gives the Stripe and Figma counts from the by-employer pivot.
expectations: run.json exists in the run directory with the target's name, linkedin_url, slug and person_id
Before the first gather agent or angle search runs, the reply to the user states the angle list, a cap per angle, and a projected credit total
Every row in final.json has at least one evidence item with non-empty text
No two rows in final.json share the same vanity slug or the same ACoAA member id
<slug>-connections.xlsx exists with tabs summary, all people, by employer, tier A, tier B, tier C and coverage
The final report gives a count for Stripe and a count for Figma, matching the by employer tab
The final report has a section listing what was not covered
No social_post_search call filters on a name column (actor.name, comments.name, reactors.name)

evals.prompt: map Satya Nadella's network from linkedin.com/in/satyanadella. I only want people who are clearly connected, so leave the weak matches out of the spreadsheet.
evals.expected_output: An exec-shaped angle set (leadership peers, board, investors, deal counterparties, press) rather than company-wide headcount, every oversized pool narrowed, and a workbook built without tier D.
expectations: The angle list includes at least one of: leadership peers, board, investors, deal counterparties, press or web footprint
No angle searches the target's employer without a function, seniority, window or team constraint
Every angle whose count query returned more than 2,000 people has a log entry stating how it was narrowed
The workbook has no 'tier D (appendix)' tab, and its summary tab still reports the tier D count
Every social_post_search filter on a crustdata_entity_id is paired with an actor_type condition

evals.expected_output: The skill recognises a company page, spends nothing, and asks for a person's LinkedIn profile URL instead.
expectations: No person_search, person_enrich, social_post_list_live or social_post_search call is made
The reply asks for a person profile URL of the form linkedin.com/in/...
No run directory, final.json or .xlsx file is created
